title: In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found
description: In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 14, “The Temple”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: In Thy courts let peace be found, Be Thy tem-ple full of love; Here we tread on ho-ly ground, All se-rene, a-round, a-bove.

lines: In Thy courts let peace be found,
Be Thy temple full of love;
Here we tread on holy ground,
While the knee in prayer is bent,
While with praise the heart o'erflows,
Be the place for worship meet,
Meet the worship for the place;
As an infant knows its home,
Lord! may we Thy temples know;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
